title: Better Than The Freezer Aisle: My Crispy Air Fryer French Toast Sticks
description: Ditch the soggy microwave sticks! These air fryer french toast sticks are perfectly golden, crisp on the edges, and soft inside. Ready in under 15 minutes.
story: It’s 7:00 AM on a Tuesday, and the rain is drumming against my kitchen window while my 'Morning Coffee' jazz playlist hums in the background. I’m usually a 'grab a granola bar' girl when things get busy, but today I needed something that felt like a hug. My little apartment kitchen smells like warm cinnamon and melted Kerrygold butter right now, and honestly, it’s the only thing getting me through my inbox. I learned the hard way that if you soak the bread for more than a couple of seconds, you end up with a soggy mess that sticks to the basket—I actually cried a little the first time I ruined a batch! Keep the dip quick. I used that thick Trader Joe’s brioche loaf because it holds up so well under pressure. These sticks are my little morning win: crunchy on the edges, custardy in the middle, and so much better than the boxed stuff I grew up with.
ingredients: 4 thick slices of Trader Joe's brioche bread, cut into 1-inch strips
1 tbsp maple syrup for the custard
Cooking spray or 1 tbsp melted Kerrygold butter for the basket
instructions: Step 1: Whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, syrup, and salt in a shallow bowl until the cinnamon clumps disappear and the mix looks like a pale sunset.
Step 2: Dip each brioche strip into the custard for just 2 seconds per side—seriously, don't let them get waterlogged or they'll fall apart in the fryer!
Step 3: Arrange the strips in a single layer in your air fryer basket, leaving space between them so the hot air can swirl around and get those edges crackling.
Step 4: Air fry at 370°F for 8 to 10 minutes, flipping them halfway through when they start to smell like a cozy bakery and look perfectly golden-brown.
proHack: For a crunch that actually snaps, lightly dust the soaked sticks with a tiny bit of granulated sugar right before they go into the air fryer. The sugar caramelizes under the high heat, creating a thin, glass-like crust that stays crispy even under a lake of syrup.
storage: Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for 2 days. To get that 'just-made' texture back, don't use the microwave—pop them back in the air fryer at 350°F for 3 minutes until they sizzle.

faqs.question: Can I use regular white bread if I don't have brioche?
faqs.answer: You can, but it's a bit flimsy. If you're out of brioche, try thick-cut Texas toast or even a stale loaf of French bread from the Aldi bakery section.

faqs.question: How do I keep the cinnamon from clumping in the eggs?
faqs.answer: Whisk the cinnamon into the eggs alone first to create a paste before adding the milk. It helps the spice distribute evenly so you don't get 'cinnamon spots' on your toast.
